meta.verification_method: Each published claim is checked against the linked public source text or structured record. Source conflicts, moving rankings and unavailable pre-event statistics are kept visible; see data/research-ledger.json and the Verified List page.
meta.notes: Counter-Strike rosters and rankings change frequently. Ranking figures are snapshots with exact dates. Live Valve (VRS) rankings on HLTV differ from Valve's last published snapshot; both are cited where relevant.
meta.verification_passes: Four passes of 20 new ledger entries each: first build and entries 1-20 on Sept 23, 2026 (pass 2, entries 21-40, same day); pass 3 (entries 41-60) and pass 4 (entries 61-80) on Sept 24, 2026. Pass 4 added the Global Qualifier deep-dive, the official-page contradiction, field absences, The MongolZ crisis, PGL Masters Bucharest and the "final VRS opportunity" conflict, EPL S24 field checks, odds status, prize-share columns and sponsor/source-independence notes. Ledger: data/research-ledger.json (80 entries).

rules.core_roster: At least 3 of the 5 players on the Aug 3, 2026 VRS roster must play, or the team takes a technical loss (2.10/3.7)
rules.roster_size: Max 8 members; the coach may stand in (3.5)
rules.stand_in: One stand-in, registered 72h before and approved 15 min before a match; an emergency stand-in may be confidential (3.7, 3.7.1)
rules.coach_comms: The coach may talk at any time (3.9.1)
rules.delays: Bo3: 15 min late forfeits map 1, 30 min forfeits the series (3.17.2)
rules.pauses: Technical pauses are time-limited; 4v5 continuation is allowed if the team has won 10+ rounds or leads by 6+ (3.17.3)
rules.server: MR12, $800 start, 1:55 rounds, 20s freeze, 40s C4, 3x30s timeouts; overtime MR3 (best of 6) with $12,500 start and 1 timeout per OT (4.1)
rules.veto_bo3: Coin toss -> A ban, B ban, A pick, B pick, A ban, B ban; decider side by knife (4.4)
rules.veto_bo5: A ban, B ban, then 4 alternating picks; decider side by knife (4.4)
rules.withdrawal: More than 20 days out: next VRS team; less than 20 days: next European VRS team (2.4.6); 72h to accept an invite (2.4.5)
rules.integrity: Betting ban for participants (2.9); Akros anti-cheat (4.5.5); 3 minor = 1 major, 3 majors = disqualification (5.1-5.2)
rules.seeding: By September VRS (Sept 7, 2026 snapshot); implied order: Falcons, Legacy, FURIA, 9z, Aurora, BetBoom, PARIVISION, Virtus.pro (inference)

irregularities.issue: Prize pool figures differ across sources
irregularities.detail: Official Thunderpick/PRNewswire: $1,115,000 total circuit with $1,000,000 for the Malta Finals. EGamersWorld/Strafe/escharts list the Finals at $500,000, and GosuGamers lists $615,000. The $500,000 figure may reflect only the club share of the $1M (HLTV splits it as $500k player share / $500k club share); GosuGamers' $615,000 matches no official figure.
irregularities.resolution: Site uses the official $1,000,000 Finals / $1,115,000 circuit figures.

irregularities.detail: Official releases say 'BLAST Studios Malta' (one PR dateline: Ta' Qali). Liquipedia lists 'BLAST Arena Studios, Attard'. Some outlets wrote 'Valletta'. All refer to the same BLAST studio venue in Malta.
irregularities.resolution: Site uses 'BLAST Studios, Malta (Attard per Liquipedia)'.

irregularities.detail: HLTV's Dec 11, 2025 article said the LAN finals would be 'October 12-19'. Final official dates are October 14-18, 2026.
irregularities.resolution: Site uses Oct 14-18 (Liquipedia, HLTV event page, official PR). Resolved further: the official site's 'Finals 2026: 12-19 October' is the arrival-through-departure window (arrival Oct 12, media day Oct 13, groups Oct 14-16, playoffs Oct 17-18, departure Oct 19) - match days remain Oct 14-18.

irregularities.detail: PRNewswire (Sept 16) listed e.g. 'Legacy #3, Falcons #4, FURIA #8'; esportbet wrote 'Falcons #2, FURIA #4'. These mix ranking systems/dates (HLTV weekly vs Valve VRS snapshots vs HLTV's live Valve ranking). Example: Legacy is #6 on HLTV's Sept 21 ranking, #6 on Valve's Sept 7 VRS snapshot, but #2 on HLTV's live Valve ranking badge (Sept 23). Verified on Sept 23: the HLTV event page badges carry both ranks - e.g., Legacy shows #6 (HLTV weekly) and #2 (live Valve); FURIA #4 / #8; Falcons #5 / #5; BetBoom #15 / #10; 9z #16 / #13; PARIVISION #19 / #23; VP #50 / #43. esportbet (Sept 16) adds a third variant: "BetBoom, 9z and PARIVISION, currently ranked 12th, 14th and 19th in the global standings" - these labels match no published snapshot (Valve Aug 3 / Sept 7, HLTV Sept 21) and are treated as unverifiable outlet labels.
irregularities.resolution: Site always labels which system and which date: HLTV World Ranking (Sept 21) and Valve VRS official snapshots (Aug 3 invite basis; Sept 7 latest published).

irregularities.detail: Valve's Aug 3 VRS snapshot lists rosters that were already outdated (FL4MUS on BetBoom, saadzin on Legacy, HObbit+slaxejezzz on PARIVISION). The TWC Finals rosters reflect the actual, current lineups.

As of the second verification pass on Sept 23, 2026, group placements and the day-by-day schedule remain TBD on Liquipedia and HLTV; only the finals-week structure (arrival/media/group/playoff days) is published on the official site.
irregularities.resolution: Marked as pending; to be updated in a future session.

irregularities.issue: No outright winner odds available at research time
irregularities.detail: esportbet's dedicated TWC betting hub still showed 'Odds for the Thunderpick World Championship are not available' at the Sept 24 fourth-pass check (its Sept 16 article: bookmakers "have yet to open outright markets"); esportsinsider's odds feed carried no futures even for the Global Qualifier. Thunderpick (title sponsor) will offer markets per their official site.
irregularities.resolution: Betting guide provides verified form/H2H data and a framework instead of live odds; links provided for manual odds checks. Re-check after Oct 3 (EPL) and before Oct 14.

irregularities.detail: 9z's and PARIVISION's official in-game-leader designations are not explicitly stated in the sources gathered (max and Jame are the veteran leaders historically associated with calling)
irregularities.resolution: Explicitly labeled 'not officially labeled' on the Players page rather than asserted

irregularities.issue: EU Series 1 winner appears under two names
irregularities.detail: Hotspawn's final report (May 31) names VRSDelivery; HLTV's prize list names DragonClaw. Liquipedia documents the rename on May 30, 2026 - same team. A related but separate item: Liquipedia logs DragonClaw's June 2 disqualification from European Pro League Series 7 pending an organizer investigation into 'suspicious activity' (a different event, not TWC).
irregularities.resolution: Site names DragonClaw (as VRSDelivery) with the rename explained; the EPL investigation is flagged as outside TWC scope.

irregularities.detail: The 2025-26 pre-karrigan period is sometimes summarized as '7 grand finals, 1 title'. The precise, source-backed read: Falcons won PGL Bucharest 2025 (Apr 13, with degster) BEFORE m0NESY joined; with m0NESY they then lost seven straight finals (IEM Melbourne, BLAST Rivals Spring 2025, EWC 2025, ESL Pro League S22, IEM Chengdu 2025, BLAST Rivals Fall 2025, BLAST Bounty Winter 2026).
irregularities.resolution: Site states the precise sequence instead of a bare count.

irregularities.issue: Rulebook is marked '[INTERNAL]' and contains stale text
irregularities.detail: The rulebook PDF is titled '[INTERNAL] ... Official Rulebook - 01.07.2026'. It still contains '2025' wording, cross-references to non-existent sections (3.8.1, 4.8.1, 4.6) and online-event wording.
irregularities.resolution: Rules are quoted by section number with this caveat. Treat the rulebook as indicative until an updated public version appears.

irregularities.issue: Site correction: BetBoom at the Cologne Major
irregularities.detail: Earlier passes said FL4MUS deputized for visa-hit d1Ledez during the Cologne Major. Valve's match-level VRS data shows d1Ledez played at Cologne and S1ren was the absent player; FL4MUS replaced d1Ledez only at IEM Atlanta.
irregularities.resolution: Corrected on teams, roster changes, betting guide and data (ledger entry 57).

irregularities.detail: Entry 37 said '$10,000 OT money at Valve Majors'. Valve's Major rulebook gives no such figure (it requires Premier defaults), while the TWC rulebook states $12,500.
irregularities.resolution: Entry 37 was rewritten and the CS2 guide now cites the TWC rulebook (entry 43).

irregularities.issue: ESL Pro League S24 ends 3 days before TWC starts
irregularities.detail: EPL S24 runs Oct 3-11 in Katowice with 7 of the 8 TWC teams (all except Virtus.pro). The EPL final is Oct 11, TWC arrival is Oct 12 and TWC matches start Oct 14.
irregularities.resolution: Flagged as a fatigue and preparation factor. Deep EPL runs mean less rest, and teams may save strats for one event. Not a rules issue.

irregularities.detail: PGL press releases (April and August 2026) give Nov 24 as the start date; the event page and venue listing say Nov 25. The Nov 2 VRS cutoff is consistent across sources.
irregularities.resolution: Site keeps Nov 25 - Dec 13 (event page) and notes the conflict.

irregularities.detail: Liquipedia's TWC 2026 format section omits the third-place match; HLTV's event page lists a Bo3 third-place decider, and prize money is split between 3rd ($100k) and 4th ($50k).
irregularities.resolution: Site follows HLTV plus the prize split (3rd and 4th paid differently, so a decider is implied).

irregularities.detail: HLTV already lists TWC 2027 (Oct 18-25, 2027) with a placeholder map pool.
irregularities.resolution: Not used; noted only so readers do not mistake it for 2026 data.

irregularities.issue: Official Global Qualifier page contradicts itself on how many teams qualify
irregularities.detail: The page states 'Four teams will earn a slot in the TWC Finals' but later says 'The winner of the Global Qualifier earns a spot in the TWC 2026 Finals (Main Event)'. HLTV's result record shows a single qualifier (Virtus.pro). The 'four teams' line appears to be stale template text (ledger entry 64).
irregularities.resolution: Site uses one slot (winner only) per the results record and the page's own trophy line; the contradiction is published as-is for manual review.

irregularities.issue: 'Final VRS opportunity' claim conflicts with PGL Masters Bucharest
irregularities.detail: esportbet (Sept 16) called TWC 'the final opportunity for participating teams to secure VRS points ahead of the Singapore Major'. But PGL Masters Bucharest (Oct 24-31) ends before the Nov 2 VRS cutoff and includes at least five TWC teams (FURIA, Legacy, Aurora, 9z, BetBoom). The claim holds only for Falcons (skipped Bucharest) and possibly Virtus.pro (ledger entry 74).
irregularities.resolution: Site wording stays 'one of the last VRS-point opportunities'; the conflict is flagged here. Betting guide treats TWC as the last VRS event only for Falcons/VP.

limitations: Match/outright odds for TWC 2026 were still not published at the fourth-pass check (Sept 24, 2026): esportbet's TWC hub showed "Odds ... are not available" and esportsinsider carried no futures. The betting analysis is a framework plus verified form data, not live prices.
The group draw and day-by-day match schedule are not yet published (only the finals-week structure is). The seed order shown is inferred from the Sept 7 VRS.
HLTV player statistics for the Finals will only exist after the event; linked for post-event review.
Head-to-head data covers all four 2026 FURIA-Falcons meetings plus the 2025 BLAST Rivals final; full H2H scraping (all 28 pairings, all maps) is future work.
Some primary sources are X/Twitter posts or Google Drive files (the rulebook) which may require login or change without notice.

Rankings move weekly (HLTV) and per snapshot (Valve). Every rank figure on the site is labeled with its system and date. The Oct 5 VRS snapshot will change the numbers but not the seeding (which uses September).

ESL Pro League S24 (Oct 3-11) results and any post-Sept 24 roster news are not captured and must be added in a follow-up pass before Oct 14. PGL Masters Bucharest (Oct 24-31) outcomes and opening odds are also uncaptured; the group draw and day-by-day schedule remain unpublished as of Sept 24.
